probes.prompt:
Situation: `/fix-all` triage, before any edit. Finding #3's fix touches `store.go`, which already holds uncommitted edits the findings did not make. No other question is open.

Question: when do you raise `store.go` with the user? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: NOW, AT-COMMIT, NEVER. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/fix-all` finished. `git log` shows 4 commits made by the run, covering findings #1-#5 (#2 and #3 shared a root cause and one commit); #6 and #7 were deferred.

Question: write the report's first line exactly, and nothing else on that line.

Situation: `/fix-all`. The user's CLAUDE.md says: "Never run git commit; leave all committing to me." The triage round asked two questions: whether finding #2 may change an exported signature, and whether the run may commit each fix. The user answered "yes, change it" to the first and nothing to the second. Every other finding is classed auto; the baseline checks are green and the tree is clean.

Question: what does the run do next? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: STOP, FIX-UNCOMMITTED, FIX-AND-COMMIT. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/fix-all`, every finding classed auto, baseline green. Fix #2 changes `auth/token.go` and adds a test in `auth/token_test.go`. The project's checks are `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (40 packages), and `make e2e`.

Question: which tests run in the command that commits fix #2? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: AUTH-PACKAGE-ONLY, ALL-PACKAGES, ALL-PACKAGES-AND-E2E. Then one sentence why.

Situation: `/fix-all` committed five fixes. The final full check run fails `make e2e`, green on the untouched tree; `git bisect` pins it on fix #3's commit, and one repair left it red. `git revert --no-commit` of that commit stops with a conflict in `store.go`, which fix #4 also edited.

Question: what do you do? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: RESOLVE-CONFLICT, ABORT-AND-REPORT-RED, REVERT-BOTH. Then one sentence why.
